definition: The amount or quantity that serves as the basis for calculating tax by applying the tax rate.
example: Please review the tax base after reflecting deductions and adjustments.
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: A tax levied on the value added in the supply of goods and services.
example: Please first confirm whether the quoted amount includes VAT.
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: The value-added tax calculated on taxable sales and the like.
example: I checked whether the output VAT total for this filing period matches the books.
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: The value-added tax a business bears in the course of purchases. Whether it is deductible varies by transaction and requirements.
example: Please distinguish whether input VAT on corporate card spending is deductible.
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: Treating input VAT as not deductible in calculating value-added tax.
example: Please keep a record of the basis for classifying this expense as non-deductible.
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: A tax document recording the supplier, recipient, supply value, tax amount, and the like of a taxable transaction.
example: Does the contracting company name match the recipient on the tax invoice?
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: A document that amends an existing tax invoice for reasons such as changes to the transaction or entry errors.
example: The return was confirmed, so I requested issuance of an amended tax invoice.
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: A tax document issued for tax-exempt transactions and the like, recording the supply value and the transacting parties.
example: As it was a tax-exempt transaction, I received an invoice rather than a tax invoice.
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: A system whereby the payer of income withholds and remits tax in advance at the time of payment.
example: Before paying the service fee, please confirm whether withholding tax applies to the income.
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: A party obligated to withhold and remit tax when paying the relevant income.
example: I confirmed who the withholding agent is for this payment.
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: A document confirming details such as the income paid and the tax withheld.
example: Please check the previous employer's withholding tax receipt for the new hire.
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: A document that an income payer submits to the tax authorities detailing the payees and income amounts.
example: Before submitting the statement of payment, I reconciled the payee information with the amounts paid.
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: The procedure of calculating the annual tax on employment income and the like and reconciling the difference with the tax already withheld.
example: Please check the items submitted in duplicate among the year-end tax settlement materials.
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: A tax levied on a corporation's income and the like.
example: Based on the closing results and tax adjustments, we prepare the corporate tax return materials.
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: An item reflecting in accounting the future tax effects arising from differences between the accounting and tax amounts of assets and liabilities.
example: I reviewed the reversal timing of the temporary differences and calculated the deferred tax.
note: This item explains a concept used in practice. Actual application should be confirmed against working conditions, contracts, accounting standards, and the rules in effect at the relevant time.

definition: The task of entering transaction details as an accounting voucher or recording them in the books.
example: Once the account titles are confirmed, please book it by the end of today.

definition: A journal entry that flips the debit and credit to cancel the effect of an existing entry in the opposite direction.
example: I reversed the incorrectly entered voucher and then re-processed it correctly.

definition: A closing that tentatively aggregates profit or loss and financial position using data before final confirmation.
example: As not all expenses had come in yet, I reported using provisional closing figures.

definition: An amount temporarily recorded because, although a receipt is confirmed, the transaction details or final account cannot be determined.
example: I recorded it as a suspense receipt until the depositor could be confirmed.

definition: An amount temporarily recorded because, although money was paid, the usage details or final account have not been determined.
example: After the business trip, please submit the documentation and settle the temporary payment.

definition: An amount held temporarily that does not belong to the company but is intended to be passed on to another person or institution.
example: I recorded the tax deducted from payroll as withheld amounts.

definition: A state or item for which a transaction's matching, settlement, or processing is not yet complete.
example: Please check the owner and processing plan for the open items remaining by month-end.

definition: The treatment of linking matching receipt/payment, receivable, and payable items to clear outstanding balances.
example: After payment matching, I cleared the relevant receivable.

definition: A practical expression for the reconciliation work of finding the cause of amount differences across books, statements, and reports and making them agree.
example: Before reporting, please tie out the ledger and summary-table numbers first.

definition: Closing entry for the relevant accounting period or restricting additional entry in the system.
example: After confirming there are no unapproved vouchers, I'll lock the close.

definition: Temporarily lifting the entry restriction through an approval procedure because corrections are needed in a closed accounting period.
example: To reflect the correcting voucher, unlock-the-close approval is required.

definition: A practical expression for reflecting a specific expenditure as an expense or attributing it to a specific department or project budget.
example: Which department's budget should this training expense be charged to?

definition: An expression for reflecting an incurred expenditure or obligation as an expense of the relevant period in the accounts.
example: The service is finished, so please book the expense this month even before billing.

definition: A practical expression for reflecting an estimated amount set aside against expected losses and the like as a provision.
example: After reviewing collectability, I will build the necessary allowance for doubtful accounts.

definition: An expression for allocating a budget or temporarily suspending its execution. The two meanings must be distinguished by context.
example: Please hold that budget until the contract terms are confirmed.

definition: A measure that halts or restricts new hiring at a company or specific organization for a period.
example: Please confirm whether approved replacement hiring proceeds even during the hiring freeze.

definition: A practical expression for an approved staffing position or the number of people that can be filled in an organization.
example: Before posting the new job opening, please check the remaining open headcount.

definition: In HR, managing the work experience, compensation, and the like so that members stay with the organization.
example: I reviewed retention measures for key talent in terms of compensation and career.

definition: In hiring, how well an applicant's working style, values, and the like match the role or the organizational environment.
example: Instead of a vague impression, please assess fit using specific examples of collaboration.

definition: The workflow of calculating pay by reflecting attendance and compensation criteria and processing deductions, payments, and related filing materials.
example: I passed this month's assignment and leave changes to the payroll administrator.

definition: A document that informs vendors of the required tasks and proposal conditions.
example: In the RFP, we first check the delivery scope and the proposal deadline.

definition: A document that presents the method of solving a problem and the plan for carrying it out.
example: In the proposal, we state the solution along with cost and schedule.

definition: The degree to which something can be carried out in terms of budget, time, and technology.
example: We set the schedule after confirming feasibility.

definition: A common opinion or agreement reached among stakeholders.
example: We aligned on a consensus regarding the scope of change.

definition: An expression for removing a planned feature or item from the current scope of work.
example: We spec'd out the add-on items from this delivery scope.
note: Here it means exclusion from the project scope. Distinguish it from the manufacturing or inspection sense of being out of specification.

definition: A backup option prepared to replace the original plan.
example: We also prepare an alternative to use when the existing schedule is difficult.

definition: An abbreviation indicating the level of performance or utility relative to price.
example: We choose equipment with good value for money by comparing the needed performance and the price.

definition: An abbreviation for the psychological satisfaction gained relative to price. It emphasizes taste and emotional satisfaction beyond function.
example: Even if the price is a bit high, the satisfaction from the design makes it feel worth it.

definition: A shortened name for Instagram. One of the social media channels for running brand content and ads.
example: We post event announcements on the official Instagram account.

definition: A shortened name for Facebook. A channel name used in work with pages, posts, ads, and the like.
example: We check the company's public news on the Facebook page.

definition: A basis for comparing results with the same period of the previous year. The comparison period and aggregation scope, whether monthly, quarterly, or annual, are kept aligned.
example: September sales rose YoY, but we also check last year's one-off sales.

definition: A basis for comparing this month's figure with the immediately preceding month. Avoid mixing a month-to-date total with a full prior month's result.
example: We split the MoM increase in labor costs into new hires and bonus payments.

definition: A basis for comparing this quarter's results with the immediately preceding quarter.
example: We analyze whether the QoQ decline in operating profit is due to seasonality or cost increases.

definition: A basis for comparing this week's figure with the immediately preceding week. The week start date and the number of days aggregated are kept aligned.
example: When comparing applicant counts WoW, we also check the number of days the posting ran.

definition: Results accumulated from the start of the fiscal year to the reference date. If the fiscal year differs from the calendar year, the start month also differs.
example: We compare September YTD expenses with the budget cumulative for the same period.

definition: Results accumulated from the first day of the month to the reference date.
example: We report MTD sales as of the 15th separately from the full-month target.

definition: Results accumulated from the first day of the quarter to the reference date.
example: We bring Q2 QTD cash inflows to the weekly treasury meeting.

definition: The one-year period that serves as the basis for financial reporting and budgeting. Depending on the company, it may differ from January to December on the calendar.
example: We align the start and end months of the FY27 budget with the overseas subsidiary.

definition: The calendar-based year from January 1 to December 31.
example: We distinguish CY-based statistics from sales on the company's fiscal-year basis.

definition: A method of viewing the combined results of the most recent 12 months counting back from a specific reference date.
example: We compare recent business scale using TTM sales as of quarter-end.

definition: The growth between a start value and an end value expressed as a constant annual compound growth rate. It differs from a simple average of year-by-year growth rates.
example: When calculating 3-year sales CAGR, we align the start and end years and the number of periods.

definition: A unit expressing the difference between two ratios. A change from 10% to 12% is a rise of 2 percentage points.
example: We write that the operating margin improved by 2%p and distinguish it from a 2% increase.

definition: A unit expressing differences in interest rates, yields, and the like; 1 bp is 0.01 percentage point.
example: We calculate how much interest expense rises if the borrowing rate goes up 25 bp.

definition: A phenomenon where the figure in the comparison base period is unusually high or low, making the growth rate appear greatly different.
example: We exclude the base effect of last year's expense reversal and explain this year's expense trend.

definition: The characteristic of results fluctuating repeatedly in particular seasons or periods.
example: We compare monthly labor costs taking into account the seasonality of bonus payment timing.

definition: A figure converted to an annual or set-period scale assuming the recent performance trend continues.
example: We show the recent monthly sales run rate separately from the confirmed forecast that reflects seasonality.

definition: Actual incurred or aggregated figures as opposed to plan or forecast. We distinguish provisional results before closing from confirmed results.
example: We reflect confirmed closing actuals rather than the forecast in the budget file.

definition: Estimating future sales, costs, profit, and the like based on current information and assumptions.
example: As the order schedule slipped, we lowered next quarter's sales forecast.

definition: An analysis that explains, by cause, the differences between actuals and budget, forecast, or past results.
example: We split the labor cost variance analysis into headcount and average salary changes.

definition: An analysis that connects the process of change from a starting figure to a final figure through increases and decreases by factor such as price, volume, and cost.
example: We show the change from last year's operating profit to this year's as a bridge.

definition: The flow of cash into or out of a company. Accounting profit and actual cash inflows and outflows can differ in timing and amount.
example: Even if the P&L is in the black, CF can fall short if collections are late.

definition: An earnings indicator before deducting interest and corporate taxes. It is not always the same value as accounting operating profit.
example: We separately disclose the adjustment items of the EBIT used in comparing investment proposals.

definition: An indicator presented by adding or subtracting specific company-defined items from EBITDA. The adjustment basis and its link to the original figure should be confirmed.
example: We report adjusted EBITDA excluding one-off costs together with the excluded items.

definition: The ratio of gross profit (sales less cost of sales) to sales.
example: We compare gross profit margin by product to check the impact of cost increases.

definition: The ratio of operating profit to sales.
example: We explain how much the operating margin fell due to the increase in outsourcing costs.

definition: The ratio of net income to sales.
example: We split the difference between operating margin and net margin into financial costs and corporate tax.

definition: The ratio of net income to shareholders' equity. It usually uses average equity as the denominator; the period and calculation basis should be confirmed.
example: We examine whether the ROE change is due to higher profit or lower equity.

definition: A ratio showing how much profit was earned using total assets. The scope of the profit and average assets is specified.
example: We review why ROA fell after the new facility investment.

definition: An indicator of profitability such as after-tax operating profit relative to the capital invested in operations. The calculation scope of invested capital is applied consistently.
example: We compare business-unit ROIC with the cost of capital to review investment efficiency.

definition: The profit attributable to one common share. Basic EPS is calculated based on profit attributable to common shares and the weighted-average number of shares outstanding.
example: We check the EPS in the results materials together with changes in profit and share count.

definition: Earnings per share reflecting the dilutive effect of securities and the like that could be converted into shares.
example: We compare diluted EPS, which includes the effect of stock options, with basic EPS.

definition: The dividend paid per share.
example: We check the total payout by reconciling the DPS in the dividend plan with the number of shares issued.

definition: The ratio of profit paid out as dividends. It is calculated by aligning the scope of the profit and dividends used.
example: We compare the payout ratio after confirming whether it is on a consolidated or separate net income basis.

definition: A value used to assess the entire business value of a company. For listed companies, it may be calculated by adjusting market capitalization for net debt and the like.
example: We align the treatment of cash and debt when converting EV to equity value.

definition: A method of estimating the value of a business or asset by converting future cash flows to present value at an appropriate discount rate.
example: In the DCF model, we check the change in value while varying the growth rate and discount rate.

definition: The sum of the present values of expected cash inflows and outflows.
example: We reflect both the initial investment and maintenance costs in the NPV of the facility investment proposal.

definition: The discount rate that makes the net present value of an investment's cash flows zero. Depending on the cash flow pattern, there may be multiple solutions or none.
example: We report not only the IRR but also the investment size and recovery timing.

definition: The cost of capital calculated by weighting the costs of equity and debt according to the capital structure.
example: We align the cash flow basis of the valuation model with the WACC basis.

definition: The period it takes to recover invested funds through subsequent cash inflows.
example: We check whether an investment with a short payback period also has high subsequent maintenance costs.

definition: An analysis that checks how much the result changes when key assumptions are varied.
example: We prepare a sensitivity analysis of profit to the exchange rate and the sales growth rate.

definition: An indicator expressing in days the average period it takes to pay trade payables. The calculation basis, such as the purchase amount, should be confirmed.
example: We check whether a falling DPO increased the working capital burden.

definition: An indicator showing the average period inventory stays before being sold or used.
example: For items with a longer DIO, we set up a separate inventory clearance plan.

definition: A working capital turnover indicator that subtracts the payable deferral period from the period during which funds are tied up in inventory and receivables.
example: We check the CCC trend by adding DIO and DSO and subtracting DPO.

definition: Current assets less current liabilities. In enterprise value analysis, operating net working capital excluding cash, debt, and the like is sometimes used.
example: We first agree on the accounts subject to NWC adjustment in the contract.

definition: The balance of cash, deposits, and the like held at a reference point. Whether restricted funds are included is distinguished.
example: We report the cash balance and the available balance separately before reflecting scheduled payments.

definition: A report organizing the day's cash and deposit balances, receipts and payments, and the funding plan.
example: We reconcile the closing balance in the daily cash report with the bank transaction details.

definition: A plan that forecasts funding shortfalls or surpluses by reflecting expected receipt and payment timing.
example: We reflect tax and payroll payment dates in the weekly cash plan.

definition: Transaction terms specifying the timing, method, and installment status of payment.
example: We check whether each supplier's payment terms are accurately entered in the cash plan.

definition: A notation for terms requiring full payment within 30 days from an agreed reference date such as the invoice issue date.
example: We confirm in the contract whether the Net 30 start date is the acceptance date or the invoice date.

definition: A processing unit that gathers payables due for payment, reviews and approves them, and then transfers them in a batch.
example: Before finalizing the payment run, we check for duplicate invoices and account changes.

definition: The work of moving funds between accounts.
example: For large funds transfers, we reconcile the approval details with the recipient account.

definition: A method whereby payments are automatically withdrawn from an account according to a set consent and conditions.
example: We share the automatic debit date and the withdrawal limit with the treasury team.

definition: A transaction that transfers trade receivables to a financial company and the like to raise funds or outsource collection management.
example: We review the accounting treatment by confirming whether the factoring contract is with recourse.

definition: A method of managing funds by concentrating or linking the balances of multiple accounts or affiliates.
example: We organize the accounts that will participate in the overseas subsidiary's cash pooling.

definition: A credit facility that allows repeated borrowing, repayment, and re-borrowing within the agreed period and limit.
example: We report the unused limit and maturity schedule of the RCF at the month-end treasury meeting.

definition: Property or rights provided to secure the performance of an obligation.
example: We reconcile the scope of the collateral set under the borrowing agreement with the asset register.

definition: Conditions agreed to be observed in a borrowing contract and the like, such as financial ratios and restrictions on actions.
example: We confirm the EBITDA definition to apply in the quarter-end covenant calculation in the agreement.

definition: A ratio showing how well earnings can cover interest expense. It generally compares operating profit and the like with interest expense.
example: We align the numerator basis of the interest coverage ratio with the loan agreement.

definition: A ratio comparing cash flow available for repayment and the like with the principal and interest repayments for the period.
example: When calculating DSCR, we confirm the scope of available cash flow per the agreement.

definition: The speed at which a business consumes cash in its operations. The gross-spending basis and the net basis (after cash inflows) are distinguished.
example: We split the cause of the rising monthly net burn rate into hiring and capital spending.

definition: An estimate of the period a business can operate based on currently available cash and the expected cash burn rate.
example: We separately calculate runway excluding new investment inflows.

definition: A procedure performed by an independent auditor to express an opinion on whether the financial statements are prepared in accordance with the applicable accounting standards.
example: We manage the owners and submission dates of the audit request materials.

definition: An activity that independently inspects the organization's risk management, controls, and operations from an internal perspective.
example: In the internal audit, we check how the payment approval procedure actually operates.

definition: Procedures and activities the organization designs and operates to ensure reliable reporting, effective operations, legal compliance, and the like.
example: We separate account changes and payment approval to strengthen internal control.

definition: An internal control system designed and operated to ensure the reliability of accounting information.
example: We ask the internal control staff to submit evidence of control performance.

definition: Dividing the tasks and authorities that must check one another to reduce errors or fraud.
example: We inspect the segregation of duties for vendor registration and payment authority.

definition: A table linking business risks with the control activities, owners, and evidence that address them.
example: We write the control performance frequency and review evidence in the RCM.

definition: An inspection that follows the flow of a single transaction to understand and confirm the procedure and control design.
example: We confirm the approval points from purchase to payment via a walkthrough.

definition: A record that allows tracing who created, changed, or approved which transaction or information, and when.
example: We check in the system whether an audit trail remains for voucher edits.

definition: A practical notation for the materials a company prepares for the auditor's review, or the list of such requests.
example: We update the outstanding items and owners on the PBC list daily.

definition: A document to have a counterparty, financial institution, and the like confirm balances and transaction facts.
example: We explain the discrepancies in the trade receivables confirmation replies using the transaction details.

definition: Purchased goods in transit. Whether to recognize them as assets is judged based on conditions such as the transfer of ownership or control.
example: We confirm goods in transit at the closing date using the delivery terms and shipping documents.

definition: A practical expression for amounts for which revenue has been recognized but an invoice has not yet been issued.
example: We check the scheduled billing date of unbilled revenue by project.

definition: An asset where the right to consideration for recognized revenue depends on conditions other than merely the passage of time.
example: For consideration with an outstanding acceptance condition, we review the distinction between contract asset and receivable.

definition: An obligation to provide goods or services for which consideration has been received from the customer or has become billable.
example: We review the contract liability corresponding to advance payments to match the service provision timing.
